name: Danish

ancestors.notes: Descent from Old Norse (East Norse branch)
Low German / Hanseatic adstrate: even stronger than Swedish due to geographic proximity and political union

notes: Standard Danish (rigsdansk). QUANTITY: a stressed vowel is long in an open syllable / before a single consonant and short before a consonant cluster or a doubled consonant letter; Danish itself has NO long consonants, so doubled letters are read as a single consonant (they only signal the preceding short vowel). This is encoded with data only: doubled letters are grapheme keys mapping to a length-marked consonant (⟨bb⟩→/bː/), consonant clusters are grapheme keys mapping to the concatenated phonemes (⟨st⟩→/sd/), the vowel-shortening allophone rules fire on `followed_by_phoneme` = those cluster/geminate phonemes, and a second set of rules degeminates /Cː/→/C/. SCHWA: unstressed ⟨e⟩ is [ə] (Grønnum 2005; Basbøll 2005) — the single most frequent segment in the language. SOFT D: /d/ after a vowel is the approximant [ð] (mad [mað], gade [ɡæːðə]). SILENT D: ⟨nd⟩→[n], ⟨ld⟩→[l], ⟨rd⟩→[ʁ]. NO ASPIRATION AFTER /s/: ⟨sp st sk⟩ → [sb sd sɡ]. R: onset ⟨r⟩ is the uvular [ʁ]; coda r-vocalisation ([ɐ̯]) is NOT encoded. A-QUALITY: /a/ retracts to [ɑ] next to /r/. H: /h/ is syllable-initial only, so ⟨h⟩ is silent in a coda and in ⟨hv hj⟩ (hvor [voːʁ], hjem [jɛm]). G-ELISION: single intervocalic ⟨g⟩ after a long vowel drops (tage [tæːə]). C: ⟨c⟩ is [s] before a front vowel (recept), [k] elsewhere. STØD is suprasegmental and is not encoded; the WikiPron/Wiktionary gold marks it (ˀ) and also writes /r/ as ⟨r⟩ rather than ⟨ʁ⟩ — both are transcription-convention differences from this spec, not errors in it. Neither gold this spec is scored against writes [ɑ] consistently — WikiPron spells it ⟨a⟩ in the large majority of tokens — so the retraction rules cost PER against notation, not against pronunciation. KNOWN GAP — ⟨ig⟩: the ⟨ig⟩ digraph (→ long [iː]) over-fires word-finally before a following vowel, so a doubled-⟨g⟩ word like ligge, kigge, tigge still surfaces with the wrong long vowel and an elided /ɡ/ (gold: lʔeɡə, kikə/kʔiɡə, tekər) instead of a short vowel with /ɡ/ retained; a word-final ⟨ig⟩ constraint is needed and is out of scope for this PR (o2i task #80: 45/65 non-final ⟨ig⟩ words over-lengthen).

/a/ is retracted to [ɑ] adjacent to /r/ (fra [fʁɑ], rar [ʁɑː]); [a] and [ɑ] are in near-complementary distribution conditioned by a neighbouring /r/ (Grønnum 2005; Basbøll 2005).
Long counterpart of DA_A_RETRACT_AFTER_R_SHORT (Grønnum 2005; Basbøll 2005).
/a/ is retracted to [ɑ] before /r/ (har [hɑː], par [pɑː]) — the mirror environment of DA_A_RETRACT_AFTER_R_SHORT (Grønnum 2005; Basbøll 2005).
Long counterpart of DA_A_RETRACT_BEFORE_R_SHORT (Grønnum 2005; Basbøll 2005).

/h/ occurs syllable-initially only (Basbøll 2005), so a coda ⟨h⟩ is silent: øh [øː], åh [ɔː]. Excludes a following ⟨y⟩: the syllabifier misclassifies the h of ⟨uhyre⟩/⟨uhyggelig⟩ as coda when it is actually onset to the following syllable (tracked as an engine defect, task #79) — this environment is narrowed to the cases where the deletion is demonstrably correct.

Single intervocalic ⟨g⟩ after a long vowel is elided: tage [tæːə], sige [siːə]. After a short vowel it is retained (bygge [byɡə]), so the rule is restricted to the long-vowel context and to the single-letter grapheme. Claim is standard (e.g. Grønnum 2005); edition not consulted.
⟨dd⟩ is the soft d as well: sidde [siðə]. Same lenition as DA_SOFT_D — doubled ⟨d⟩ only signals the short vowel, it does not block the approximant (Grønnum 2005; Basbøll 2005).

Danish short stressed high/mid vowels lower in a large, partly-conditioned class that keeps the spelling of the historical higher vowel: against the WikiPron gold, stressed ⟨i⟩→[e] in 111 words, ⟨y⟩→[ø] in 61, ⟨u⟩→[o] in 64, and ⟨ø⟩→[œ] in 68 (near-categorical before ⟨r⟩). til [ˈtel] is one instance (Grønnum 2005; Basbøll 2005). This entry is a SEED LIST pinning a frequent member of the class, not the full generalisation; the conditioned environment for the rest of the class is tracked as follow-up (o2i task #80).

nul [ˈnol] lowers its historical /u/ to [o] while keeping the ⟨u⟩ spelling (Grønnum 2005; Basbøll 2005) — one of 64 stressed ⟨u⟩→[o] words in the WikiPron gold; SEED LIST member, see DA_LEXICAL_LOWER_TIL (o2i task #80 tracks the full class).

kys [ˈkøs] lowers its historical /y/ to [ø] while keeping the ⟨y⟩ spelling (Grønnum 2005; Basbøll 2005) — one of 61 stressed ⟨y⟩→[ø] words in the WikiPron gold; SEED LIST member, see DA_LEXICAL_LOWER_TIL (o2i task #80 tracks the full class).

søn [ˈsœn] lowers its historical /ø/ to [œ] while keeping the ⟨ø⟩ spelling (Grønnum 2005; Basbøll 2005) — one of 68 stressed ⟨ø⟩→[œ] words in the WikiPron gold, near-categorical before ⟨r⟩; SEED LIST member, see DA_LEXICAL_LOWER_TIL (o2i task #80 tracks the full class).
